role.altitude: The industrial ecologist keeps framing studies, inspecting sources, interpreting results and persuading managers; copying emission figures from reports, rebuilding scenario spreadsheets, preparing input-output tables by hand and compiling waste figures from invoices shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An ecologist whose analyses rerun when data change, leaving time for interpretation and persuasion.

tasks.short: Plan the study, gather historic process and emission data, build projected-change scenarios, analyse the ecological implications of changes in industrial processes or development, and write the study report.

steps.what: Ecologist plans the study: scope, questions and methods
Ecologist gathers historic process and emission data for the industrial site or region
Ecologist builds scenarios for projected changes in industrial processes
Ecologist analyses the ecological implications of the changes
Ecologist writes the study report

tasks.design: Historic emission figures come by query from the national emission register and the organisation's environmental database, instead of being copied from annual report PDFs. Scenarios are built as a parameterised life cycle model, so a projected change is a new parameter set and the result tables refresh, instead of a new spreadsheet. Planning and analysing the implications stay with the ecologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were copied from reports and each scenario was a new spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Emission registers and parameterised life cycle models.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which projected change matters for the local ecosystem.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and rebuilding; analysis stays.

evidence.claim: A life cycle tool supports parameterised models and refreshes report tables when the model changes.
Emissions and waste are reported annually on the government environmental report form.

assumptions: Boundary: studying ecological implications; technical reports (task 19978) and forecasting ecosystems (task 16895) are sibling tasks.
s5 is part of preparing technical and research reports, which sibling task 19978 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s2: emission data held in the national register and the database kept through task 16894, for about 70% of the figures needed; s2 is priced at that share.
Planning and analysing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of historic data available electronically.
research_questions: Do studies cover more scenarios in the same time?

incremental.description: Ecologist keeps the parameterised model current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: old paper data; high: register data and repeat scenarios.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify candidate sources, pull emission and monitoring data, inspect and measure sources, attribute impacts, research methods of pollution abatement or control, and record findings.

steps.what: Ecologist identifies candidate sources of pollution
Ecologist pulls emission and monitoring data for the sources
Ecologist inspects the sources and takes measurements in the field
Ecologist determines the environmental impact of each source
Ecologist researches methods of pollution abatement or control in reference documents
Ecologist records findings and candidate methods with their sources

tasks.design: Emission and monitoring data for the candidate sources come by query from the emission register and the organisation's environmental database, instead of being collected from separate reports. Findings go into a source register with links to the data used. Identifying sources, field inspection, determining impacts and choosing abatement methods stay with the ecologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were collected from separate reports for each source.
tasks.enabler_now: Emission registers and environmental databases queried by source.
tasks.still_hard: Diffuse sources with no reported data.
tasks.human_edge: Smelling or seeing a leak no register shows.

evidence.claim: Emissions and waste are reported annually on the government environmental report form.

assumptions: Boundary: researching pollution sources; reviewing research literature (task 19982) and recommending protection methods (task 19963) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: data held in the national register and the database kept through task 16894, for about 70% of sources; s2 is priced at that share.
s5 keeps its full time; reading reference documents does not change.
Identifying, inspecting and determining impacts keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sources with reported data.
research_questions: Are sources identified in fewer site visits?

incremental.description: Ecologist keeps the source register current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: diffuse sources; high: many reported point sources.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define the question, prepare input-output tables and environmental extensions, map spend or output to sectors, run the input-output analyses, check and interpret the results, and document the method.

steps.what: Ecologist defines the question and system boundary
Ecologist prepares the input-output tables and environmental extensions
Ecologist maps the spend or output to economic sectors
Ecologist runs the environmentally extended input-output analyses
Ecologist checks the results for plausibility and interprets them
Ecologist documents the method, data versions and choices

tasks.design: A script downloads the published multi-regional input-output tables and environmental extensions, aggregates them to the needed sectors and region, and records the data version, instead of the ecologist preparing them in spreadsheets. A concordance table maps purchase or product categories to sectors, and the ecologist reviews only unmapped lines. The script runs the matrix calculation and contribution analysis reproducibly. Defining the question and interpreting results stay with the ecologist; the method note lists data versions and settings from the script.
tasks.previous_blocker: Large tables were handled by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Scripted pipelines over published input-output tables.
tasks.still_hard: Products that do not fit sector averages.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a large result comes from a mapping error, not the economy.

ambition.what: Rerun the analysis each year when new tables are published.

tasks.altitude: Much less table handling; interpretation stays.

reach.learn: Whether hotspot results are updated yearly.

evidence.claim: Scripted pipelines and report templates handle repeat data preparation deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: input-output analyses; material flow analyses (task 19968) and flows of materials and energy (task 19970) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: published input-output tables and extensions are released in a stable format; each new release needs a script check.
Input contract for s3: the concordance table built once from earlier analyses covers about 70% of spend categories; s3 is priced at that share.
Defining and interpreting keep their full time.
research_questions: Are analyses rerun with each new data release?

incremental.description: Ecologist updates the script and concordance when tables change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off analyses with new sector mappings; high: repeat analyses on the same tables.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess current practices with managers, prepare the waste and resource case, present environmental management systems to managers and staff, provide guidance, and follow up adoption.

steps.what: Ecologist assesses current environmental practices with managers
Ecologist prepares figures on waste, energy and water use and their costs
Ecologist promotes environmental management systems to managers and staff
Ecologist provides guidance documents for system procedures
Ecologist follows up adoption with the managers

tasks.design: Waste, energy and water figures come from a dashboard fed by supplier invoices and meter data, instead of the ecologist compiling them from invoices in a spreadsheet. Agreed actions go on a shared action list with owners, so follow-up is a filtered view. Assessing practice, promoting the system and the guidance stay with the ecologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resource figures were compiled from invoices by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reporting tools that extract figures from invoices with an audit trail.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a manager that the system pays for itself.

reach.learn: Whether managers adopt sooner with their own figures.

evidence.claim: A sustainability reporting tool extracts figures from invoices and keeps an audit trail.

assumptions: Boundary: promoting environmental management systems; technical materials for managers (task 16883) is a sibling task.
s4 is part of providing technical materials to industrial managers, which sibling task 16883 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s2: invoices and meter data reach the reporting tool through finance, for about 70% of sites; s2 is priced at that share.
Assessing and promoting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sites with meter data.
research_questions: Do more sites adopt a management system?

incremental.description: Ecologist checks dashboard figures against a sample of invoices.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small sites without meter data; high: many metered sites.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
